note: Curated from the Btown Brief newsletter vault (editions Jun 22 - Jul 17, 2026). Refresh by pulling chat-worthy headlines from recent editions and phrasing them as natural openers.

points.text: Did you hear Burlington made a national top-towns-to-visit list? Number six.
The Vermont Green women made a playoff run in their first season ever. Anyone catch a match at Virtue Field?
There's an official Vermont creemee passport now. Road trip?
Front Porch Forum just turned twenty. What's the wildest thing you've seen on there?
A Stowe mansion got auctioned off with no minimum price. What would you have bid?
Ben & Jerry's Foundation says it's shutting down over the fight with their parent company. Feels like the end of an era?
Beta keeps getting bigger — campus, jobs, all of it. Where do you think that goes?
Turns out Italian American families have been farming Colchester for a hundred years. Did you catch that story?
A land trust just bought two thousand acres in the Champlain Valley to keep it wild.
The Nostalgia toy store on Church Street is closing. Did you ever wander in?
Leunig's is opening a spot in South Burlington's City Center. Good move or is it a Church Street thing?
Kountry Kart is doing late-night again. What's your order?
Vermont game stores are turning into little clubhouses — chess nights, card leagues, all of it. Would you go?
The Champlain Parkway finally opened. It took sixty-one years. Have you driven it yet?
Apparently Noah Kahan fans keep making a Vermont road sign disappear. Did you hear about that one?
If a tourist gave you one day in Burlington, hour by hour, where do you send them?
Vermont's officially rethinking air conditioning as summers heat up. How are you surviving?
Seven Days spent twenty-four straight hours on Church Street. What do you think 3 AM looks like out there?
Some guy is filming all one hundred of Vermont's covered bridges for YouTube. How many do you think you've crossed?
Lippa's Jewelry left Church Street after ninety-three years. What shop would you miss most?
The mayor says Burlington is back. Agree or not?
One of the papers asked if Vermonters are hungry for neighborhood connection. Well — are we?
